query: The Second Bout The money-holder points at the chalk again. {~A lanky girl steps in who quit the academy last spring. She kept the wand, and the duelling stance.|A fairground conjurer steps in, still in spangles, rolling a spark across his knuckles. The crowd knows him.|A hedge-hexer from past the village steps in, a cord of knotted charms at her wrist. Some of those knots aren't legal anywhere.} {flag(ring_last_standing): Last standing: there's no stepping out now.|The purse has doubled. Or you can take what you've won and go.} Fight on {~She duels by the book she walked out on. You've read the later chapters. Her wand ends up in the crowd, and the purse ends up heavier.|The conjurer's sparks are all show. You aim at the hand that isn't waving, and he sits down in a shower of spangles.|You cut her charm-cord with your first spell. Whatever the knots were for, it doesn't happen, and she spits and yields.} {~She was the best in her year before she left, and she still is. She helps you up off the flagstones, which is worse.|He palms a spark, and while you watch it, the other hand ends the bout. You limp up the steps with the night's winnings and singed sleeves.|One knot comes undone, and something cold walks through your head. You come round outside, with your purse, and a headache that lasts a day.} Take the purse and go {~You bow out with the purse in your fist. The dropout shrugs and finds someone else.|You leave the conjurer to the next fool, and count your winnings on the walk home.|The hexer laughs as you go, and ties another knot.}

results.title: Frost in the Chalk
results.excerpt:
Frost in the Chalk
The cellar goes cold. The lanterns shrink. A girl in white furs steps into the chalk and frost creeps out from her boots across the flagstones: Ilse Dumont. "They said the academy's best come down here," she says. She looks you over. "They lied. But you'll do."
